aiVerification.summary: The draft identifies a comparable voltage-level test but is not verified because the changed factor, baseline/test conditions, evidence citations, and sample/count interpretation need correction.
issues: Changed factor is incorrectly set to the filename instead of the tested voltage condition levels for S-MG.
Baseline and changed conditions are left as not explicit even though row Sheet1!26 labels 2000 V as Normal, suggesting it may be the baseline against 1800 V and 1600 V.
Change domain 'dimension/spec' is unsupported by the cited evidence; this appears to be a process/test-condition voltage comparison with gauss measurement outcomes.
Key context/header rows Sheet1!17 and Sheet1!18 are not included in the review-case evidenceRows, reducing citation clarity for the outcome metric and columns.

Rows Sheet1!21 and Sheet1!22 appear to contain continuation sample values for the 1600 V condition but are not cited; similar continuation rows may exist for 1800 V and 2000 V outside the provided context.
SubResult sampleCount values of 1 are misleading because the report states Q'ty check 50 and shows multiple sample measurements per condition.
correctionPlan: Rename the changed factor to the tested S-MG voltage level comparison, e.g. 'Voltage S-MG level: 2000 V Normal vs 1800 V vs 1600 V'.
Set 2000 V(Normal) as the baseline condition if no contradictory source context exists, and set 1600 V and 1800 V as changed/test conditions.
Change the domain to a more appropriate process/test-condition category rather than dimension/spec.
Add Sheet1!17 and Sheet1!18 to evidenceRows for the outcome title and column definitions.
Include continuation sample rows for each voltage condition where present, or limit the cited evidence explicitly to summary rows containing average/max/min.
Correct or remove misleading sampleCount values unless the true per-condition sample count can be validated from the workbook.
aiVerification.evidencePolicy: Current citations prove the existence of the voltage summary rows but are insufficient for final evidence because header/context rows and continuation sample rows are incomplete.
